title: Overall score delta mixes score change with coverage change
body:
## Summary
The scan timeline shows an overall delta between scans that covered different module sets.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/ProjectHealthDashboard/ScanHistoryTimeline.tsx:29 subtracts overallScore of adjacent reports; src/lib/evaluator/scan-report.ts:73 averages over the modules covered so far, and coverage grows across scans. A newly scored weak module moves the mean with no module getting worse. Distinct from the recorded eval-harness deviation (judge drift). Fixed means the delta compares the shared module set, or says coverage changed.

## Flow
- Scan A covers 3 modules at 100
- Scan B adds a fourth at 40 and leaves the 3 unchanged
- Timeline shows a red -15

## Expected impact
Designers stop reading a coverage gain as a regression. Could break: delta values shown today change.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - delta reflects only modules present in both scans
Before: walked case: 3 modules at 100, fourth added at 40, delta -15 with 0 modules worse
After: same case: delta 0 on the shared set, plus a coverage note
Method: simulation - one case walked through scansToReports; the rung above needs the product choice between shared-set delta and a labelled delta
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: fixture of two scans with differing coverage asserting the rendered delta on both arms

title: Discrepancy banner compares project cells with global judge verdicts
body:
## Summary
QualityDiscrepancyBanner joins project-scoped module cells to judge verdicts from every project.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/AggregateQualityDashboard/QualityDiscrepancyBanner.tsx:26 fetches /api/judge-verdicts with no project; src/app/api/judge-verdicts/route.ts:64 lists all verdicts and src/lib/status/judge-verdicts-db.ts has no project column. The cells beside it come from the project-scoped roll-up, so project B can be told its content failed on the strength of project A's verdicts.

## Flow
- Judge fails content while project A is open
- Open project B with healthy matrix quality
- Banner names B's module as disagreeing

## Expected impact
The truth-surfacing banner stops raising false alarms across projects. Could break: existing verdicts have no owner to migrate from.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - banner signals belong to the open project
Before: 0 of 2 sources share a scope: cells are project-scoped, verdicts are not
After: 2 of 2 scoped
Method: simulation - read of both paths; a change needs a verdict-table scope column, which is out of this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: architecture
instrument: two-project DB fixture asserting the banner per project

title: Discrepancy banner keeps pre-review verdicts after refresh
body:
## Summary
The banner loads verdicts once on mount and ignores the dashboard's refresh and batch-settled re-derive.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/AggregateQualityDashboard/QualityDiscrepancyBanner.tsx:31 runs load once; src/components/modules/evaluator/AggregateQualityDashboard/index.tsx:74 fetchData refreshes the aggregates and history only. After a batch review or Refresh, cells update while verdicts stay as mounted, so the disagreement list can be stale until the tab remounts.

## Flow
- Open Quality
- New judge verdicts land or a batch review settles
- Press Refresh: cells change, banner verdicts do not

## Expected impact
The banner agrees with the data beside it after Refresh. Could break: one more fetch per refresh.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - banner refreshes with the dashboard
Before: 1 of 3 reads (aggregates, history, verdicts) is left out of fetchData
After: 3 of 3
Method: simulation - read of the refresh path; needs a refresh-signal prop decision on the banner
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test counting verdict fetches after Refresh on both arms

title: Heatmap status counts are distinguished by color alone
body:
## Summary
Each heatmap cell prints three bare numbers whose meaning is only their color.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/AggregateQualityDashboard/HeatmapGrid.tsx:240 renders done, partial and missing as unlabelled colored spans, and the legend above covers quality only. WCAG 1.4.1 and the repo's StatusToken guidance both ask for more than hue; a screen reader hears three numbers inside the cell's button name.

## Flow
- Open Quality with reviewed modules
- Read a cell's footer without color or with a screen reader
- Three unlabelled numbers

## Expected impact
Colorblind and screen-reader users can read the counts. Could break: dense cell footer needs a layout check.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - counts readable without hue
Before: 0 of 3 counts labelled per cell
After: 3 of 3
Method: simulation - counted in source; choice between glyphs and sr-only text needs a visual check in the running app
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: DOM assertion on accessible text plus a screenshot of a dense cell on both arms

title: Module detail opens out of view from the lower panels
body:
## Summary
Picking a module in Needs Attention or Stale Reviews opens a detail panel that sits above them.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/AggregateQualityDashboard/index.tsx:296 renders ModuleDetailPanel above WorstModulesPanel and StaleReviewsPanel, and neither row scrolls to it, so on a page taller than the viewport a click appears to do nothing.

## Flow
- Scroll to Stale Reviews
- Click a module row
- Detail opens above the fold with no scroll or focus move

## Expected impact
Row clicks visibly answer. Could break: a scroll on heatmap clicks would be unwanted, so it must apply to the lower panels only.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - selecting a row shows its detail
Before: 2 of 2 lower panels open the detail out of view when the page exceeds one viewport
After: 0 of 2
Method: simulation - layout read from source; jsdom has no layout, so a browser walk is the instrument
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
instrument: Playwright walk asserting the panel is in viewport after a row click
